resumen: Lying on the bench, the bar comes down to the chest and is pressed back up. It is the reference horizontal push for chest, triceps and front delts.
ejecucion: Set the safety pins at chest height, or have someone spot you: getting stuck under the bar is the serious accident in this lift.
Lie on the bench with your feet on the floor and your shoulder blades pinched against the bench.
Grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders, wrists straight, and unrack it until it sits over your shoulders.
Lower the bar to your chest under control, elbows about 45-60 degrees away from your torso.
Press the bar up until the arms are straight, without lifting your back off the bench.
When the set is done, bring the bar back to the rack and make sure it is resting before you let go.
matices: What shifts the balance between chest, triceps and front delt is the bench angle: that is what the cited study measured, with a fixed grip. What happens when the grip changes, that work does not say.
